🇲🇽🏭 <u>Minimum Wage Now Buys 1.9 Food Baskets, Up From 0.8 in 2018</u>

Labor Secretary Marath Bolaños presented the "Labor Spring" numbers. The minimum wage rose from 88 pesos a day in 2018 to 315 in 2026, a 154% real recovery. In 2018 it bought 0.8 basic food baskets; today it buys 1.9. The share of people working more than 48 hours a week fell from 27.1% in 2020 to 22.2% in 2025, and the road to a 40-hour week starts with 46 hours in 2027.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Oaxaca: Mixtec Community Defender Shot Dead</u>

Humberto García Cruz was a community defender in Santa Cruz Itundujia, Oaxaca, and a member of Sembrando Vida. On September 21 he was shot several times as he and his wife returned from their plot. She survived by throwing herself to the ground. He accompanied neighbors whose rights had been violated as they sought help from the authorities. Cedhapi is demanding that the Oaxaca State Prosecutor's Office find those responsible and protect his family.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's Religious Right: From the Cristeros to the PAN</u>

In Contralínea, Pablo Moctezuma Barragán traces the line: the Sinarquistas, Los Tecos, MURO, El Yunque, and the PAN cadres they fed, a link that went public under Fox and Calderón. In 2008, PAN Jalisco governor Emilio González Márquez pledged 90 million pesos of public money to a Cristero martyrs' shrine. The first 30 million had to be returned after protests. It's the same "God, Country and Family" script used by Milei, Kast and Trump, and it's aimed straight at the Reform Laws.

🇲🇽📜 <u>Sheinbaum: Undoing the 4T's Rights Takes Two-Thirds of Congress</u>

Sheinbaum says rolling back the social rights written into Mexico's Constitution over eight years of 4T government would be "very complex" in the short term: any force that tries would need a two-thirds majority. She called the current legislature the "Constituent Congress of the Fourth Transformation." It brought Pemex and CFE back as public companies, recognized Indigenous peoples, and made welfare programs constitutional rights.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Ayotzinapa: 12 Years On, the Case Stays Open</u>

Mexico's government presented its new Ayotzinapa report today. It sets four priority lines of investigation, including a fresh analysis of the cellphones used in Iguala on the night of September 26–27, 2014, plus new searches and new arrests. Deputy Interior Secretary Arturo Medina and special prosecutor Mauricio Pazarán delivered it. Sheinbaum was blunt: presenting progress "is not closing the investigation."

‍LATIN TIMES: Why Mexico and Brazil Are Both Refusing Trump's Military Playbook in South America September 27, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Latin Times reported the UN split straight. More than a dozen governments joined Trump's anti-cartel "Shield of the Americas." Mexico and Brazil, the region's two largest economies, stayed out. Lula and Sheinbaum are quoted in their own words next to Trump's. The refusal is presented as a sovereignty position grounded in international law, not as being "soft on cartels." • "Brazil does not belong in anyone's backyard" (Lula) • "The ISIS of the Western Hemisphere" (Trump, on cartels)

text: ‍PIIE: After two years, where is Mexico heading under President Sheinbaum? September 28, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Former IMF Western Hemisphere chief Alejandro Werner lays out the numbers: 3.26% inflation, exports to the US up 42% in two years, an average US tariff on Mexican goods of just 3.7%, and ~70% approval. Then the verdict: a project of "consolidating something close to one-party rule." 🇲🇽 The growth line, "weakest in Latin America, except for Venezuela, so far this century," covers 26 years, and 18 of them were PRI and PAN governments. • "The economy has preserved macroeconomic stability while growing very little" • "This short-term equilibrium merely delays Mexico's challenges"

‍BREITBART: Mexico Confirms 'Historic' Cartel Fuel Seizure Was 'Flawed' September 28, 2026 | 🔴 📰 Breitbart treats Harfuch's announcement as proof that its own earlier scoop was right, and as evidence of a government "manufacturing raids and seizures." 🔍 What it skips: the federal review is what caught the anomalies. The FGR's Guanajuato delegate, Juan Francisco Vera, was fired, and the 59-million-liter case went to the organized-crime prosecutors (FEMDO). Harfuch announced all of this himself on Sept 25. Harfuch is never quoted directly. His admission is paraphrased to fit the thesis. • "manufacturing raids and seizures in an attempt to divert attention" • "government continues to protect the political elite"
banner: Breitbart spins fuel-raid firing as cover-up

text: ‍NEWSWEEK: Migrant Caravan From Honduras Heads Toward US Border September 28, 2026 | 🟡 📰 The headline says a 600-person caravan "heads toward US border." The article says it's in Tapachula, Chiapas, "hundreds of miles" away, and that Border Patrol apprehensions are running 94% below the Biden-era average. 🔍 Quoted: DHS, the US Embassy in Honduras, Nancy Mace, Marjorie Taylor Greene. Mexican officials quoted: zero. The caravan is walking through Mexico, but nobody asked Mexico what happens next. • "closely engaged with its international partners" (DHS) • "We have not seen a caravan… in several years, why now?" (MTG) • "no leaders beyond 'hunger' and 'necessity'" (migrant José Zelaya)
